Estimate which month the snapshot describes. Use only the figures supplied plus your general knowledge of economic history.

Reply with one JSON object and nothing else:

Rules: year is an integer from 2007 to 2026; month is an integer from 1 to 12; c in [0, 1] is your confidence that the guess is within 6 months of the truth; 1 to 3 short cues citing the inputs.
text:
This looks like late 2017. The fed funds rate is about 1.16%, which fits the period after the June 2017 hike and before the December 2017 hike. The unemployment rate is 4.4%, and the 10-year yield is 2.30%.

Headline CPI at 1.65% year over year is low, consistent with the summer of 2017. Core CPI at 1.71% fits as well, since it was about 1.7% in June to August 2017. The VIX at 10.29 and emerging-market equity up 6.3% in one month point to a calm, strongly rising market.

The 3-month change in headline CPI of -0.74 means CPI was about 2.4% three months earlier. In February 2017 it was 2.7%, and in March it was 2.4%. So the snapshot would be June 2017, when CPI was 1.6%.

Other June 2017 readings are less consistent. Unemployment was 4.3% in June 2017 (and 4.4% in May as first published), and the fed funds average was 1.04% in June and 1.15% in July. Fed funds at 1.16% points to July 2017 or August 2017. Unemployment was 4.3% in July 2017 and 4.4% in August 2017 (later revised). The 10-year yield was 2.30% in July 2017 and 2.12% in August 2017, but the unemployment rate of 4.4% may reflect a vintage difference.

Emerging-market equity was up 6.3% in July 2017, which matches. The dollar fell sharply in the 3 months to July 2017, which also fits. I'll pick July 2017.
